title: FluencyCraft Advanced - Day 08
why_important: Handling crisis communications protects company reputation.

questions.question: Day 8 Practice (Corporate Governance & Crisis (Phase 2)): When talking about asking for item weight price (every morning), which sentence is grammatically correct for 'Our neighbor'?

options.a: Apples kg how much cost? yesterday
options.b: Apples kg how much cost?
options.c: How much are these organic apples per kilo?
options.d: I am asking for item weight price right now.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option C
Natural everyday English uses standard tense agreement: "How much are these organic apples per kilo?".

questions.question: Day 8 Practice (Corporate Governance & Crisis (Phase 2)): When talking about declining an out-of-scope task (on weekends), which sentence is grammatically correct for 'The delivery executive'?

options.d: While I understand the urgency, our current bandwidth is full.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option D
Natural everyday English uses standard tense agreement: "While I understand the urgency, our current bandwidth is full.".

questions.question: Day 8 Vocabulary (Corporate Governance & Crisis (Phase 2)): What is the exact practical meaning of the phrase 'iron out'?

options.a: To perform a daily task hastily without preparation.
options.b: Resolve minor problems or details in a plan.
options.c: To clean or inspect a physical room thoroughly.
options.d: To postpone or cancel an activity indefinitely.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option B
'iron out' means: resolve minor problems or details in a plan. Example: "We need one final sync to iron out contract details."

questions.question: Day 8 Vocabulary (Corporate Governance & Crisis (Phase 2)): What is the exact practical meaning of the phrase 'reach out to'?

options.a: To clean or inspect a physical room thoroughly.
options.b: Contact someone for help or information.
options.c: To perform a daily task hastily without preparation.
options.d: To postpone or cancel an activity indefinitely.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option B
'reach out to' means: contact someone for help or information. Example: "I will reach out to customer support tomorrow."

questions.question: Day 8 Vocabulary (Corporate Governance & Crisis (Phase 2)): What is the exact practical meaning of the phrase 'run errands'?

options.a: To postpone or cancel an activity indefinitely.
options.b: To perform a daily task hastily without preparation.
options.c: To clean or inspect a physical room thoroughly.
options.d: Do short daily trips for chores.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option D
'run errands' means: do short daily trips for chores. Example: "I need to run errands at the market before dinner."

questions.question: Day 8 Vocabulary (Corporate Governance & Crisis (Phase 2)): What is the exact practical meaning of the phrase 'pick out'?

options.d: To clean or inspect a physical room thoroughly.

questions.explanation:

'pick out' means: carefully choose specific items from a group. Example: "Could you help me pick out the best mangos?"

questions.question:
Day 8 Translation Scenario 1 (Corporate Governance & Crisis (Phase 2)):

Telugu: "సాయంత్రం మా ఇంటికి రండి, టీ తాగుదాం."
(Literal attempt: "Evening my house come, tea drink.")

options.a: I am needing to evening my house come, tea drink.
options.b: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.
options.c: Please drop by our home this evening; we can have tea together.
options.d: Evening my house come, tea drink.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option C
Natural Version: "Please drop by our home this evening; we can have tea together."

Use 'drop by our home' for informal invitations.

questions.question:
Day 8 Translation Scenario 2 (Corporate Governance & Crisis (Phase 2)):

Telugu: "ఈ ఒప్పందంలో కొన్ని మార్పులు చేస్తే బాగుంటుంది."
(Literal attempt: "In agreement some changes if do good.")

options.a: It would be advantageous to incorporate a few revisions into this agreement.
options.b: In agreement some changes if do good.
options.c: I am needing to in agreement some changes if do good.
options.d: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option A
Natural Version: "It would be advantageous to incorporate a few revisions into this agreement."

Use executive diplomacy 'It would be advantageous to...'.

questions.question:
Day 8 Translation Scenario 3 (Corporate Governance & Crisis (Phase 2)):

Telugu: "మీ ఆలోచన బాగుంది కానీ మన బడ్జెట్ దానికి అనుమతించదు."
(Literal attempt: "Your thought good but budget not allow.")

options.a: While your proposal is insightful, our current budget constraints prevent us from adopting it.
options.b: I am needing to your thought good but budget not allow.
options.c: Your thought good but budget not allow.
options.d: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option A
Natural Version: "While your proposal is insightful, our current budget constraints prevent us from adopting it."

Use diplomatic contrast 'While your proposal is insightful...'.

questions.question:
Day 8 Translation Scenario 4 (Corporate Governance & Crisis (Phase 2)):

Telugu: "అన్నా, బస్టాండ్ దగ్గర డ్రాప్ చేయండి, ఎంత అవుతుంది?"
(Literal attempt: "Brother bus stand drop me, how much will become?")

options.a: I am needing to brother bus stand drop me, how much will become?
options.b: Please drop me off near the bus stand. How much is the fare?
options.c: Brother bus stand drop me, how much will become?
options.d: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option B
Natural Version: "Please drop me off near the bus stand. How much is the fare?"

Avoid 'how much will become' and ask 'How much is the fare?'.
